While remodeling occurs at the maxillary tuberosity (resorption on the anterior surface and apposition on the posterior surface), the primary mechanism for creating space for permanent molars is the posterior growth of the maxilla through apposition of bone on the posterior surface of the tuberosity, which effectively moves the tuberosity posteriorly. C) The zygomaticomaxillary sutures contribute to increase in height and length of the maxilla. This statement is correct. Growth at the circummaxillary sutures, including the zygomaticomaxillary sutures, is a major mechanism for the downward and forward displacement of the maxilla, which directly contributes to its increase in both height and length.
D) The intermaxillary suture closes about eight years postnatally. This statement is incorrect. The intermaxillary (midpalatal) suture typically remains open and active for growth throughout childhood and adolescence, often not fully fusing until the late teens or early twenties.

Based on the evaluation, option C is the most accurate statement regarding the postnatal growth of the maxilla.
